job: Revising a widely-cited orchestration leaderboard's reporting schema to capture per-task wall-clock and cost alongside accuracy scores.
outcome: A published benchmark column that formalizes latency/cost-per-task as a standard reported axis for multi-model orchestration parity claims.
motivation: Accuracy-only tables let router-as-a-model systems claim frontier parity while hiding a ~30-minute wall-clock tax, eroding the benchmark's credibility.

task.what: Add per-task time-to-completion and cost columns to scoring
task.where: The leaderboard's evaluation harness and results schema
task.when: Between June 2026 and Q1 2027, ahead of the next benchmark refresh
task.why: So parity claims cannot hide a wall-clock tax
task.how: Instrumented per-task timers plus a standardized cost-per-task rubric

job: Running real-world end-to-end tests of orchestration models on practical tasks and publishing wall-clock observations that contradict accuracy-parity claims.
outcome: Widely-cited evidence that orchestration latency is material, pressuring evaluators and vendors to adopt time-to-completion disclosure.
motivation: Vendor leaderboards overstate practical usefulness; surfacing the wall-clock gap protects readers and builds the evaluator's authority.

task.who: The independent evaluator and their testing workflow
task.what: Time end-to-end runs on standard practical task suites
task.where: Personal shader, interactive-scene, and reasoning test setups
task.when: Through the runway from June 2026 into early 2027
task.why: To prove accuracy parity hides a wall-clock tax
task.how: Stopwatch-style end-to-end timing on repeatable task batteries

job: Pricing and positioning a learned-router product against frontier models, deciding whether to publish wall-clock SLAs to defend parity claims.
outcome: A vendor-published time-to-completion or wall-clock SLA that makes latency a disclosed, contractual reporting axis.
motivation: Independent tests undercut bare accuracy-parity marketing; disclosing SLAs reframes the slower-but-better tradeoff as a feature buyers can underwrite.

task.what: Define and publish per-task wall-clock SLA tiers
task.where: Product pricing pages, model cards, and docs
task.when: Across the runway from launch through Q1 2027
task.why: To defend parity claims against latency criticism
task.how: Tier-based latency targets backed by internal benchmark telemetry
